summary: Checkpoint CP4. Adversarial subagent review of the checker returned: core C2/C4 and file-existence/sha logic sound, all 18 rev1 findings independently re-derived and true for pinned 82b96a7d, but 10 defect classes found (path alias/escape, .json + canonical ledger discovery, directory provenance, status-blind severity, duplicate-id shadowing, evidence truthiness, cycle gap, broken exit-code contract, narrow selftest, snapshot staleness). v3 ships fixes for 1-8 and 10 with the selftest widened from 4 to 11 controls (7 negative, 4 positive), now 11/11 PASS. Live provenance drift found on pinned revision 43135049: evaluation_rubric.yaml is fa4aa6c7 in the lead-audit ledger event but 25808142 on disk -> 1 hard C3; plus 17 warns (6 missing/empty outputs on in-progress nodes, 1 file with no provenance event, 10 nodes with no class_ids) and 12 C4b info. v2 already cleared the reviewer's live .json false positive; verified against comms/outbox/e08_artifact_map_gate.event.json. No node completed; claimed_completion=false.
expected_information_gain: Converts the gate tool from a single-worker claim into a red-teamed control: the defects that would have produced false C3 findings or missed escapes are now closed and regression-tested, so leads can rely on its verdicts for done-node gating.
next_falsifier: A second reviewer (different worker, not the same subagent) reproduces the 11 selftest controls and re-derives the rev5 hard finding from the file and the lead-audit event; any misclassification reopens the checker.
A different reviewer must reproduce the counterexamples; same-model red teams share blind spots and are not independent verification.
note: Report is verbatim; independence limit stated in its header (same model family, same session, one agent removed).

next_falsifier: Second reviewer attempts the reviewer's counterexample table against v3; any reproduced false positive/negative reopens the checker.
change_log: v2 -> v3: canonical path normalisation (alias false C3 fixed), C0b hard for absolute/.. /symlink escapes, recursive dir content, C3 for directory provenance, C6 duplicate ids, C7 cycles, C8 field coercion warnings, status-aware severity (hard only for done) except sha mismatch which is always hard, case-insensitive sha, exit code 2 for all input/handler errors, default event sources comms/outbox + research_map/events.jsonl, evidence must be a non-empty string ref, 11 selftest controls

note: Pinned map revision 43135049; artifact existence evaluated against the filesystem at run time, so only the map is pinned.

v1 event path matching was exact-string: './schemas/x.yaml' and absolute spellings produced false C3
v1 accepted absolute artifact paths and '..' escapes, and followed symlinks out of root (false negatives)
v1 required no passed event for directory artifacts (2 live nodes use dir artifacts)
v1 applied hard C0/C1 gates to active/queued nodes, inflating the hard count
v1 silently shadowed duplicate node ids and mis-parsed string depends_on
v1 crashes exited 1, indistinguishable from verdict=fail, contradicting its exit-code contract
v1 selftest exercised only C1/C3/C4 and bypassed load_events/main
findings: All 18 rev1 hard findings were independently recomputed and are true for pinned 82b96a7d; the core file-existence and C2/C4 logic is sound

Disposition: defects 1-8 and 10 fixed in v3, each with a regression control (11 controls, 11/11 PASS); defect 9 resolved by widening the selftest; defect E (legit '._payload.json' hidden by the junk filter) retained by repo convention and documented as a limitation

Residual gaps accepted and recorded: evidence_refs are presence-checked not resolved; directory contents are not hashed without a manifest; snapshot pins map JSON but not the filesystem; mismatch severity on an 'unverified' artifact event is a judgement call (hard) that lead-audit may downgrade
Not independent verification: same model family, same session, one red-team agent; a different reviewer is required before the checker is treated as trusted
next_falsifier: A different execution worker (not flash-19, not its subagent) runs the 11 controls and the counterexample table; verdict moves off revise only then.

summary: Residual limitation recorded during final verification, no verdict change: norm_rel canonicalises symlinks, so the new symlink artifacts/audit/evaluation_rubric.yaml -> ../../evaluation_rubric.yaml and the root path evaluation_rubric.yaml resolve to the same provenance key. This correctly unifies alias spellings (reviewer defect 2) but conflates a symlink with its target: if the link is repointed, recorded hashes are compared against the new target. The rev5 hard finding (lead-audit event audit-artifact-rubric-20260911T231931 records fa4aa6c7, file hashes 25808142) is genuine under either reading. Future runs should either record the symlink path as a distinct key or hash the target with an explicit link note.
next_falsifier: Repoint the symlink to a different file and re-run; if the A0 provenance finding follows the new target with no separate finding for the link path, the conflation is confirmed. If two distinct findings appear, the limitation is closed.
expected_information_gain: Prevents a future reviewer from mis-reading a symlink-target hash change as tampering; documents the exact canonicalisation semantics of the gate.
